big: An AIF is a privately pooled fund for sophisticated investors, with a usual minimum of ₹1 crore. SEBI sorts AIFs into three categories, and the category tells you what kind of risk the fund may take.

lines: Because the risks differ. Category I backs the economy, like start-ups and infrastructure. Category II covers private equity and debt funds without leverage beyond daily needs. Category III uses complex strategies and may use leverage.
